assertion: New York City's public schools lost about 23,000 students, or nearly 3%, from the year before, according to preliminary numbers the Education Department released Monday.
independent_value: NY1 (Nov 16): 766,900 K-12 as of Oct 31, down 23,000 or 2.9%. Preliminary figure.
measure: school district enrollment New York City public schools

assertion: That leaves the nation's largest school system with about 766,900 students, from kindergarten through senior year, as of Oct. 31.
Over the past decade, the city has lost about 200,000 students, or nearly 20%.
inaccuracy: The claim says 'nearly 20%'; the evidence (NY1: 964,132 in 2016-17 to 766,900) is -197,232, or -20.5%, which is just over 20%.

assertion: When the city's free preschool programs for 2-, 3-, and 4-year-olds are included in the enrollment tally, the total is 863,100, according to the Education Department's preliminary data. That was down about 2.6% from the previous year.
Since 2020, New York City has spent nearly $2 billion to prop up budgets at schools with declining enrollment.
independent_value: Chalkbeat June 22, 2026: nearly $1.9 billion since 2020 (about $290 million next year).

assertion: By the 2034-35 school year, the city is predicting that the student population will fall by another 130,000, according to demographic projections from the School Construction Authority.
reason: Projection (estimate): SCA Table A1 shows 849,652 in 2025-26 falling to 721,251 in 2034-35, a decline of 128,401, i.e. about 130,000. Caveat for readers: SCA counts PK-12 excluding District 75, measured from 2025-26.
measure: school district enrollment New York City public schools
why_no_page: SCA PDF read in full via the article's signed link; the storage host root returns HTTP 400 and lists no index page.

assertion: Thirty states have seen public school enrollment declines since 2014.
warehouse_value: NCES CCD district sums 2014 vs 2024: 31 of 51 jurisdictions (states + DC) declined
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT state_abbr, "year", SUM(CASE WHEN enrollment>0 THEN enrollment END) e FROM edu.ccd_districts WHERE "year" IN (2014,2024) AND fips BETWEEN 1 AND 56 GROUP BY state_abbr, "year") SELECT COUNT(*) states, SUM(CASE WHEN b.e<a.e THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) declined FROM s a JOIN s b ON a.state_abbr=b.state_abbr AND a."year"=2014 AND b."year"=2024
inaccuracy: The claim says 30 states; the warehouse count is 31 of 51 jurisdictions (includes DC, ends 2024); NYT page returned HTTP 403 so the cited source was not read directly.

assertion: Historically, when schools have fewer students than projected on their roster, the Education Department claws back money in the middle of the school year. But since the pandemic, the city has largely kept school budgets steady despite enrollment declines.
independent_value: Chalkbeat June 22 and June 7, 2026 pieces describe the same midyear clawback practice and the hold-harmless exception since 2020.

assertion: Enrollment in city-funded preschool programs was up slightly.
The preschool increase came thanks to the rollout of a new program for 2,000 2-year-olds this year as well as an uptick in 4-year-olds signed up for prekindergarten programs.
source_finding: Chalkbeat Sept 10 confirms roughly 2,000 toddlers started 2-K. The 4-year-old uptick was not independently verified; 2,000 new seats exceeds the net +240, so other preschool categories fell.

assertion: Mamdani's free 2-K program expects to add 10,000 more seats next year.
independent_value: Chalkbeat Oct 19: program growing to 12,000 kids next year from 2,000 this year = +10,000.

assertion: Several contributing factors lead to the drop: falling birth rates, families leaving the city, and a slowdown of immigration into the five boroughs under President Donald Trump.
source_finding: City Comptroller report (via NY1) cites lower births, decreased migration in and families moving out; Chalkbeat Nov 19 shows steepest losses in immigrant-heavy districts and schools.
independent_value: Comptroller report and district patterns; stated as contributing factors, no decomposition.

assertion: The city is floating proposals to close two small schools in Harlem and one in Brooklyn, as well as merge two sets of schools in the Bronx and Brooklyn, expected to be voted on by the Panel for Educational Policy over the next two months.
independent_value: Chalkbeat Nov 2: two Harlem closures (112 and 40 students), vote Dec. 16; Chalkbeat Nov 19: five closure/merger proposals on PEP agendas Jan 20 and Jan 27, 2027, consistent with 3 closures + 2 mergers.

assertion: "We've started to have conversations in communities," Samuels told the Chancellor's Parent Advisory Committee last week.
speaker: Kamar Samuels
reason: No other page located containing the quote; Chalkbeat's Nov 2 piece quotes Samuels on small schools but not this line.
why_no_page: Fetched Chalkbeat Nov 2 and NY1; neither contains the quote; the meeting has no public transcript found.

assertion: The declines in New York City mirror national trends. Many large school systems, including Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia and Houston, are also grappling with sharp drops.
warehouse_value: 31 of 51 jurisdictions lower in 2024 than 2014 (NCES CCD)
independent_value: Chicago -11,500 (Chalkbeat Sept 24); Philadelphia about -2,500 (Chalkbeat Oct 20); Houston about -9,000 to -10,000 (Houston Public Media); LAUSD lost 300,000+ over two decades (NPR).
